hypotheses.statement: solang rejects the blockhash() builtin at compile time ('unknown function or type') while solc accepts it, so any contract using blockhash diverges via COMPILE_ASYMMETRY regardless of runtime arguments.

evidence.note: solang emitted two 'unknown function or type blockhash' errors at lines 10 and 16; solc compiled cleanly.

hypotheses.next_probe: Minimal contract with a single function `function h(uint n) public view returns (bytes32) { return blockhash(n); }` — confirm solang compile fails and solc compile succeeds, isolating blockhash from other env vars.

hypotheses.statement: solang rejects tx.origin at compile time ('builtin tx.origin does not exist') while solc accepts it; pallet-contracts has no origin/caller distinction exposed to Solidity.

evidence.note: solang error 'builtin tx.origin does not exist' at line 20 in senderIsOrigin(); no runtime steps could execute due to compile failure.

Isolated contract using only tx.origin: solang failed with 'builtin tx.origin does not exist' at both use sites (line 7 view getter, line 11 mutating record) while solc compiled cleanly. Rejection is attributable to tx.origin alone and occurs in both read and write contexts.

hypotheses.next_probe: Contract with only `function o() public view returns (address) { return tx.origin; }` — verify solang compile failure is attributable to tx.origin alone.

hypotheses.statement: solang accepts msg.sender, block.number, and gasleft() on pallet-contracts (they produced no compile errors in the same file where blockhash and tx.origin failed), though runtime values may still differ from EVM semantics.

evidence.note: solang's error list mentioned only blockhash and tx.origin; msg.sender (lines 20, 25), block.number (lines 10, 16), and gasleft() (line 11) parsed without complaint, but no runtime comparison was possible.

hypotheses.next_probe: Contract using only msg.sender, block.number, gasleft(), block.timestamp, and msg.value in view/mutating functions; compile with both toolchains and compare returned values against anvil to test whether agreement is syntactic only or also semantic.
